body.statement: Characterize the sharp region \(\mathfrak F\) of exponent triples \((a,b,c)\in[1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\) for which the primitive class \(\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\), with global signal \(\psi=\sigma_r(M)\asymp n^a\), local comparability \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\), \(g\asymp n^b\), \(H\asymp n^c\), and \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\asymp n^{-1-\min\{b,c\}}\), permits oracle-scale curvature-corrected native-optimizer inference. Derive raw bounds for every native-transfer, centered-quadratic, cubic, penalty, covariance-plug-in, Hessian-plug-in, and weight-plug-in remainder as functions of \(n,g,H,\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\); after exponent substitution, define \(\mathfrak F\) exactly by the resulting affine inequalities that make every remainder divided by \(s\) vanish. On every compact subset of its interior, prove \(s^{-1}|(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), \(s^{-1}|Q-B_2|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), \(s^{-1}|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), \(s^{-1}|\widehat B_2-B_2|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), and \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\), together with the studentized limit. For every exterior boundary face, construct a relatively open rank-one Gaussian \(q\)-dependent family with \(|G_n|\asymp n^b\), \(|W_n|\asymp n^c\), and \(\inf_{i,t}\sigma_1(R_{it}M)/\sigma_1(M)>0\), satisfying the remaining primitive conditions, on which one named native-optimizer error is not \(o_{\mathbb P}(s)\).
body.justification: The sufficient proportional-cohort envelope is useful but does not locate the statistical or algorithmic boundary when signal, cohort, and window exponents all vary.
body.gap: Existing papers provide separate sufficient weak-factor conditions or bias-aware impossibilities, not a matched native-optimizer frontier over the exponent-indexed class with the two-component oracle variance scale.
body.consumer: The frontier determines whether a desired Tick Size post window must be shortened, the treated cohort subdivided, or the reported interval declared unsupported.

obligation.what_is_open: The raw cohort-dependent native-optimizer bounds, their complete finite system of affine exponent inequalities, and matching exterior Gaussian witnesses for every face.
obligation.obstruction: The only displayed native rates belong to the proportional-cohort theorem and remain unproved there. They contain no derived dependence on a sparse growing cohort, and no primitive argument supplies the requested necessity witnesses; declaring their conditional substitution to be sharp would assume the crux.
obligation.attempted: Proved frontier score diffuseness and the conditional score-CLT reduction, then substituted the conjectured proportional-cohort rates into the declared oracle scale to expose the inequalities they would generate. This does not certify sharpness or transfer those rates to the frontier class.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(d=\min\{b,c\}\), so the declared frontier variance has \(s\asymp n^{-(1+d)/2}\).  If the bounded-aspect raw rates displayed in the native-transfer target extended uniformly to the frontier class, exponent substitution would give
\[
 \frac{\ell_n^4}{\psi\sqrt n\,s}=\ell_n^4n^{d/2-a},
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell_n^4\sqrt n}{\psi^2s}=\ell_n^4n^{1+d/2-2a},
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell_n^4n^{-3/2}}s=\ell_n^4n^{-1+d/2}.
\]
With \(m\asymp n\) and the asserted reconstruction rate, the covariance plug-in term has the first of these polynomial exponents up to logarithms.  Thus those conjectured rates would at least require the affine inequalities
\[
 a>\frac d2,
 \qquad 2a>1+\frac d2,
 \qquad d<2,
\]
of which the middle inequality is the binding one on the declared exponent box.  This is only a conditional reduction: the frozen core supplies neither the \(g\)-dependent native-transfer, Hessian, and weight-plug-in rates nor exterior Gaussian witnesses.  It therefore does not determine a sharp region \(\mathfrak F\).
